claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys are governed by localized internal-strain heterogeneities.
Localized strain heterogeneities pin the magnetostructural phase boundary.
Moderate post-deposition annealing partially relieves residual stresses in the alloy.
Partial residual-stress relief reduces the hysteresis of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Partial residual-stress relief slightly broadens the entropy-change peak.
The as-deposited alloy is a single-phase ordered hexagonal FeMnNiGeSi alloy.
The as-deposited alloy has high internal residual stresses and strain heterogeneities.
Rapid solidification produces localized residual stresses and heterogeneous internal strain.
Strain gradients act as pinning sites during the magnetostructural transformation.
Pinning by strain gradients induces a sharp and hysteretic transition.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation eases movement of the phase boundary.
The annealed alloy will have a smoother and less hysteretic magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
The annealed alloy will have a broader entropy-change peak than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing may reduce the peak magnetocaloric effect.
Annealing is expected to improve low-field functional performance by making cooling cycles more reversible.
The predictions apply only while annealing avoids significant grain growth, phase decomposition, or unwanted phase separation.

contradictions.description: The target is repeatedly labeled 'as-deposited,' but its production is identified as arc melting/melt spinning. Melt spinning can produce rapidly solidified ribbons, whereas arc melting produces bulk ingots rather than a deposited state; the hypothesis therefore conflates distinct processing forms and does not clearly define the target specimen.
